title: Deep decimal digits and bit-level structure: where each generator stops being random, and the hidden identities in its bits
summary: I computed the exact decimal digits $d_p$, $p=1$ to $60$, of $10^8$ outputs per generator, using integer arithmetic on the exact dyadic value $m/2^B$. I compared them with the generators' intended rational values and with the naive $\mathrm{mod}(\lfloor x\,10^p\rfloor,10)$, in both double and REAL*4. An exact resolution model, the noncentrality $\lambda_p$ of the digit chi-square, predicts every observed breaking depth. A uniform $B$-bit source first fails at $p\approx B-11$ for $N=10^8$, so RAND fails at 10, R250 at 21, MT19937 and RANNUM at 42, and any REAL*4 value at 13. That is far deeper than the naive estimate $B\log_{10}2$. The exact rational digits of MINSTD never fail, while naive extraction fails for every generator at $p=16$ in double and $p=8$ in REAL*4, a pure arithmetic artifact. RANDU and RANDM have decimal digits that are exactly periodic with period $2^{30-p}$, which makes the chi-square too small (left-tail $p$ down to $10^{-11}$) at $p=5$ to $14$ and then too large from $p=17$, in four-figure agreement with theory. At the bit level I derived and verified the exact periods $2^{30-j}$ and lag-1 correlations of the LCG bits; RANDU bits 16 to 27 have $r\approx 1/3$ because $65539\equiv 3 \pmod{2^{16}}$. Berlekamp-Massey gives linear complexities of exactly 250 (R250), 19937 (MT19937) and $2^{29-j}+1$ (RANDU bit $j$). Three-term XOR tests show that R250 obeys its recurrence in all 32 bits with zero violations, that a blind scan of 179,700 lag pairs rediscovers exactly its lags (103, 250) and (206, 500), that the logistic map's output is a one-bit shift of the previous output in its top 26 bits with zero violations, and that MINSTD doubles copy bits 1 to 22 into bits 32 to 53. Along the way I found that the logistic map from seed 777 enters a 5,638,349-step cycle, and that gfortran RAND is exactly $\lfloor (k-1)/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$, which corrects the stated rule in 1/512 of draws.

methods.name: Exact decimal digit extraction (stored value)
methods.description: Every double $x\in[0,1)$ is an exact dyadic rational. The program writes $x=m\,2^{-B}$ with $m$ odd: $m$ = int(scale(fraction(x),53)) with trailing zero bits removed, and $B=53-\mathrm{exponent}(x)-t$. The digits come from the exact recurrence $r_0=m$, $r\leftarrow 10r$, $d_p=\lfloor r/2^B\rfloor$, $r\leftarrow r \bmod 2^B$, in integer(8) for $B\le 59$ and integer(16) otherwise. It was validated against Python big-integer and Fraction arithmetic on $10^5$ draws of MT19937, RANDU and MINSTD at $p\in\{1,5,10,15,16,20,30,45,52,53,54\}$: all counts are identical. A useful lemma follows from the construction: for $x=k/2^B$, the digit $d_p$ depends only on $k \bmod 2^{B+1-p}$, because adding $2^{B+1-p}$ to $k$ adds $2\cdot5^p\equiv 0 \pmod{10}$ to $x\,10^p$.
methods.parameters: N = 1e8 draws per generator, p = 1..60, seed 777 (MIDSQ 12345678, LOGISTIC also N = 1e7); double (rng_single=.false.) and REAL*4 (rng_single=.true.) runs

methods.name: Intended (rational) digits
methods.description: For MINSTD the intended value is $k/(2^{31}-1)$, with $k$ taken from rng_state_int; digits come from $r\leftarrow10r$, $d=\lfloor r/M\rfloor$, $r\leftarrow r-dM$. For MIDSQ the intended value is $k/10^8$. For every other generator the stored double is exactly the intended value. The program also records the mismatch rate between stored and intended digits.

methods.name: Naive floating-point digit extraction
methods.description: $d_p=\mathrm{mod}(\mathrm{int}(x\cdot10^p),10)$, the way a student would code it. In double, $10^p$ is exact and the product is rounded to 53 bits ($p\le18$). In REAL*4 the product $x_4\cdot 10^p$ is formed in single precision ($p\le12$). The mismatch rate against the exact digit is recorded at each $p$.

methods.name: Digit-frequency chi-square with signed two-tailed significance
methods.description: $\chi^2_p=\sum_{d=0}^{9}(n_d-N/10)^2/(N/10)$, compared with $\chi^2_9$. The signed significance is $S=+\log_{10}(1/p_{\rm right})$ when $p_{\rm right}<p_{\rm left}$ and $S=-\log_{10}(1/p_{\rm left})$ otherwise, so both non-uniform ($S>0$) and too-uniform ($S<0$) counts are flagged. A cell is anomalous when $|S|>4$ ($p<10^{-4}$, about 0.15 expected false alarms over all cells). The first failing position is the smallest $p$ with $S>4$.
methods.parameters: 9 dof; upper critical value 33.72, lower 0.661 at 1e-4

methods.name: Exact resolution model for the digit test
methods.description: Let $\pi_d(p)$ be the exact digit distribution implied by the output lattice. Then $\chi^2_p$ follows a noncentral $\chi^2_9(\lambda_p)$ with $\lambda_p=10N\sum_d(\pi_d-0.1)^2$ and mean $9+\lambda_p$. Three cases were computed exactly. (i) Uniform $B$-bit source $k/2^B$: $\pi_d=c_d/2^{B+1-p}$ with $c_d=\lceil (d+1)2^{B-p}/5\rceil-\lceil d\,2^{B-p}/5\rceil$, so $\lambda_p$ depends only on $B-p$ and grows by about $4\times$ per position. (ii) RANDU and RANDM: enumerate the full residue orbit $\{r \bmod 2^{32-p}: r\equiv1,3 \pmod 8\}$. When the digit period $2^{30-p}\ll N$ the statistic is deterministic and $\chi^2_p\approx\lambda_p$. (iii) REAL*4: enumerate all floats $m/2^{24+k}$, $m\in[2^{23},2^{24})$, binades $k=0..33$, weighted $2^{-(k+1)}$. The predicted break is where the power $P(\chi^2_9(\lambda)>33.72)$ approaches 1.

methods.name: Per-bit frequency and lagged autocorrelation
methods.description: The bits $b_j=\lfloor x2^j\rfloor \bmod 2$, $j=1..53$, are read exactly from $m=x\cdot2^{53}$ (bit $j$ is integer bit $53-j$). Frequency test: $z=(n_1-N/2)/\sqrt{N/4}$. Lagged correlation at $L=1,2,4$: $r=(\overline{b_nb_{n-L}}-f^2)/(f(1-f))$ with $z=r\sqrt N$. Bits that never change are reported as constant (dead or stuck) rather than tested.
methods.parameters: N = 5e7 per generator, double and REAL*4; MINSTD rechecked with N = 2e8 for seeds 777 and 4242

methods.name: Exact bit and digit periods of RANDU and RANDM
methods.description: Derivation: with $a\equiv3 \pmod 8$ and odd seed, the order of $a$ modulo $2^m$ is $2^{m-2}$ and $a^{2^{m-3}}\equiv1+2^{m-1}$. So $x_{n+P/2}\equiv x_n+2^{m-1} \pmod{2^m}$: bit $m-1$ flips at half period, which fixes its period at exactly $2^{m-2}$. For $x=k/2^{31}$, bit $j$ is state bit $31-j$, giving period $2^{30-j}$ for $j\le28$, with bit 29 constant, bit 30 of period 2 and bit 31 constant. The digit $d_p$ depends only on $k \bmod 2^{32-p}$, so its period is $2^{30-p}$, and at half period it obeys $d_p(n+2^{29-p})\equiv d_p(n)+5 \pmod{10}$. Verification: (a) first return times of $x_n \bmod 2^i$ over the full orbit ($2^{29}$ steps) plus a flip check at half period; (b) brute-force minimal period of each bit $i=0..22$ and each digit $p=8..30$ on $2^{23}$ consecutive states; (c) the half-period digit identity counted over all $n$.
methods.parameters: seed 777; full orbit 536,870,912 steps; 8,388,608 stored states; MINSTD as control

methods.name: Full-period theory of bit autocorrelation
methods.description: The lag-1 correlation of output bit $j$ for RANDU and RANDM is computed exactly by enumerating the residue orbit modulo $2^{32-j}$ ($r\equiv1,3 \pmod 8$) and correlating the top bit of $r$ with the top bit of $a\,r \bmod 2^{32-j}$. For large moduli this tends to about $1/a'$, where $a'$ is the multiplier's small representative (the square-wave Fourier argument gives $1/a$ for integer $a$).

methods.name: Three-term XOR identity tests
methods.description: For every bit position $j$ the program counts the $n$ that violate (i) the R250 recurrence $b_j(n)\oplus b_j(n-103)\oplus b_j(n-250)=0$; (ii) the tent-map shift identity $b_j(n)\oplus b_{j+1}(n-1)\oplus b_1(n-1)=0$, which follows from $\theta_{n+1}=1-|1-2\theta_n|$, the exact conjugate of $4s(1-s)$ under $\theta=(2/\pi)\arcsin\sqrt s$; (iii) the MINSTD copy identity $b_{j+31}=b_j$, which follows from the binary expansion of $k/(2^{31}-1)$ having period 31. All generators are tested, so each identity has 8 controls whose expected violation rate is 1/2.

methods.name: Blind lag-pair XOR scan
methods.description: With 32-bit words $w(n)=\lfloor x2^{32}\rfloor$, compute $F(s,t)=\sum_n\mathrm{popcount}(w(n)\oplus w(n-s)\oplus w(n-t))$ for every $1\le s<t\le600$. Bits that are constant over the sample are masked, and the null is $F\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n_bL,1/2)$, giving $z=(F-n_bL/2)/\sqrt{n_bL/4}$. Pairs with $|z|>5$ are listed, and the spread of all 179,700 $z$ values is compared with $N(0,1)$.
methods.parameters: T = 600, L = 20,000 words, 179,700 pairs per generator

methods.name: Berlekamp-Massey linear complexity
methods.description: The GF(2) Berlekamp-Massey algorithm finds the shortest LFSR that generates a single bit stream $b_j(0..n-1)$ and records the profile $L(n)$. A random stream follows $n/2$; a stream from a linear recurrence of order $k$ saturates at $k$ once $n>2k$.
methods.parameters: L = 50,000 bits; streams: R250 j=1,32; MT j=1,32,53; RANNUM j=1,53; MINSTD j=1,31,53; RAND j=1,22; RANDU j=1,14,16,18,20,24,28; RANDM j=1,16,20,24; LOGISTIC j=1,40,53; MIDSQ j=1

methods.name: Cycle detection and RAND reconstruction
methods.description: Brent's algorithm was run on a bit-exact replica of the logistic map state (checked against rnglib for $10^6$ steps), and the full middle-square orbit was enumerated. The gfortran RAND() output was compared, for $10^8$ draws, with three candidate formulas built from the MINSTD state $k$: $\lfloor k2^{22}/M\rfloor/2^{22}$, $\lfloor k/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$ and $\lfloor (k-1)/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$.

findings.claim: Validation: in exact arithmetic the good generators have uniform decimal digits down to $p=41$, and the test does not flag them before the depth predicted by their 53-bit resolution.
findings.evidence: N = 1e8. MT19937 and RANNUM pass every position $p\le41$ (smallest p-value 0.007, RANNUM at p = 41 with $\chi^2=22.6$; MT19937 at p = 41 has $\chi^2=17.9$). Exact-digit counts were reproduced independently in Python for MT19937 (numpy RandomState(777) reproduces rnglib MT exactly), RANDU and MINSTD.

findings.claim: For a uniform $B$-bit output $k/2^B$ the digit frequency test first fails at $p\approx B-11$ when $N=10^8$ (in general $p^*\approx B-\tfrac12\log_2N+1.3$), not at the naive $B\log_{10}2$. The exact noncentrality model predicts the measured $\chi^2$ at every depth.
findings.evidence: First failing p (exact digits, $S>4$): RAND ($B=22$) p = 10 ($\chi^2=44.7$, predicted mean $9+\lambda=32.8$, power 0.43; p = 11: 109 vs 152); R250 ($B=32$) p = 21 (136 vs 152); MT19937 p = 42 (166 vs 152); RANNUM p = 42 (174 vs 152). Deep agreement: RAND p = 15: 36,600 vs 36,609; R250 p = 24: 6,130 vs 6,109. Naive $B\log_{10}2$ = 6.6, 9.6, 16.0. Each position deeper multiplies $\lambda$ by about 4.

findings.claim: The decimal digits of RANDU and RANDM are exactly periodic: $d_p$ has period $2^{30-p}$ and obeys $d_p(n+2^{29-p})\equiv d_p(n)+5 \pmod{10}$. As a result the digit test is too uniform at $p=5$ to $14$ and deterministically non-uniform from $p=17$, in exact agreement with the full-period theory.
findings.evidence: Measured minimal digit periods equal $2^{30-p}$ for p = 9..28 (brute force on 8,388,608 states). The half-period identity holds for 100% of tested n (for example 8,372,224 of 8,372,224 at p = 15). $\chi^2$ at p = 5..12 is 0.017 to 0.076 (expected 9; left-tail p from 1e-8 down to 9.6e-12 at p = 10, S = -11.0); at p = 13, 14 it is 0.327, 0.560 (theory 0.326, 0.559). First right-tail failure p = 17, $\chi^2=83.45$ (theory 83.45); p = 19: 1,335 (theory 1,335). RANDU and RANDM agree to 0.3% for $p\ge15$ because both multipliers are $\equiv3 \pmod 8$ and sweep the same residue set.

findings.claim: Storing any output in REAL*4 caps uniform decimal digits at $p=12$ for every generator with at least 24 bits, as predicted by the binade-enumeration model. RAND is unchanged because its 22-bit values fit exactly.
findings.evidence: REAL*4, N = 1e8: first failure at p = 13 for RANDU, RANDM, MINSTD, R250, RANNUM and MT19937 ($\chi^2$ = 54.8, 34.4, 50.8, 56.7, 43.7, 49.5; predicted mean 53.1, power 0.93); p = 14: 140 to 164 (predicted 157); p = 15: 732 to 820 (predicted 715). RAND first failure stays at p = 10. RANDU's too-uniform band shrinks to p = 5, 6.

findings.claim: Naive digit extraction $\mathrm{mod}(\lfloor x\,10^p\rfloor,10)$ breaks for every generator, including MT19937, at $p=16$ in double and $p=8$ in REAL*4. This is a property of the test arithmetic, not of the generators. Below those depths individual digits are often wrong but the errors are unbiased, so the frequency test cannot see them.
findings.evidence: Double p = 16: $\chi^2\approx9.85\times10^5$ for all generators, with even digits about $1.099\times10^7$ against odd $9.0\times10^6$, because $x\,10^{16}>2^{53}$ for $x>0.9007$. REAL*4 p = 8: $\chi^2\approx6.9\times10^7$, with even digits $1.83\times10^7$ against odd $1.68\times10^6$, because $x\,10^8>2^{24}$. MT19937 mismatch rates against exact digits (double): 4.0e-4 (p = 13), 4.1e-3 (14), 0.039 (15), 0.35 (16). Yet naive p = 15 still passes (S = -0.8). REAL*4 mismatch is 0.22 at p = 7 while that position still passes.

findings.claim: Null result: the exact rational digits of MINSTD, $k/(2^{31}-1)$, are uniform at every position up to 60, because $d_p$ is the leading digit of another MINSTD stream $10^{p-1}k \bmod M$. The double that stores it is correct only to 15 or 16 digits, and its digits fail at $p=42$ like any 53-bit dyadic.
findings.evidence: Intended digits: no $S>4$ for p = 1..60 (largest $\chi^2=17.1$ at p = 60, p = 0.047). Stored double: first failure p = 42 ($\chi^2=67$, S = 10.2). Stored-vs-rational digit mismatch: 1.9e-4 (p = 13), 0.018 (p = 15), 0.19 (p = 16), 0.90 for p >= 18.

findings.claim: The logistic-map generator collapses onto a short cycle in double precision. It is the cycle, not the digits, that makes it fail the digit test at $N=10^8$.
findings.evidence: Brent's algorithm on the exact state (seed 777): tail 14,324,259 steps, then a cycle of 5,638,349 steps (about 15 repetitions within 1e8 draws). N = 1e8 fails at every p (p = 1: $\chi^2=86.7$, S = 14.1). The first 1e7 outputs (before the cycle) pass every p <= 43 (|S| <= 1.6 for p <= 25) and first fail at p = 44.

findings.claim: For MIDSQ, the gap between the intended value $k/10^8$ and its double shows up directly in the digits: the rational has only zeros beyond digit 8, the double has zeros or nines, and naive extraction mixes them in a third proportion. As a negative control, the generator fails at $p\ge2$ because it sits on a 100-step cycle.
findings.evidence: Seed 12345678: tail 10,352, cycle 100 (seed 777 collapses to 0 after 2 steps). At p = 9..16 the intended digit is 0 in 100% of draws, the stored double gives 0 in 49.0% and 9 in 51.0%, and naive extraction gives 97.0% 0 and 3.0% 9 (p = 9). Naive digits are wrong in 44% of draws at p = 4..16 because the cycle values have trailing zeros. $\chi^2=2.5\times10^7$ at p = 2.

findings.claim: Every low-order bit of RANDU and RANDM has an exactly computable short period: bit $j$ of $k/2^{31}$ has period $2^{30-j}$ for $j\le28$, bit 29 is stuck at 0, bit 30 alternates and bit 31 is stuck at 1. Bits 32 to 53 of the double are dead.
findings.evidence: Measured on the full orbit ($2^{29}$ = 536,870,912) and by brute force on $2^{23}$ states: periods 1, 2, 1, 4, 8, ..., 2^21 for state bits 0..22, and residue return times $2^{i-2}$ for $i=3..31$, with the half-period flip confirmed for every bit $j\le28$. Frequency test: bit 29 and bit 31 give $z=\mp7071=\mp\sqrt{N}$ (N = 5e7). Bit 30 lag-1 correlation = -1.000. MINSTD control: no bit period up to $2^{21}$ in its 23 lowest bits.

findings.claim: RANDU's bits 16 to 27 have lag-1 autocorrelation close to +1/3 (bit 15: -1/3). The cause is that $65539\equiv3 \pmod{2^{16}}$: the low 16 state bits evolve by multiplication by 3. The exact full-period theory reproduces the measurement to six decimals. RANDM (with $6539\equiv11 \pmod{128}$) shows the alternating pattern $+\tfrac12,-\tfrac14,+\tfrac18,\dots$. A lag-1 test alone misses period-4 bits.

Linear complexity exposes the GF(2)-linear generators exactly: every R250 bit stream is generated by a 250-bit LFSR, every MT19937 bit stream by a 19937-bit LFSR, and RANDU bit $j$ by one of length $2^{29-j}+1$. RANNUM (nonlinear scrambler), MINSTD, RAND and LOGISTIC look random.

R250 satisfies $b_j(n)\oplus b_j(n-103)\oplus b_j(n-250)=0$ in every one of its 32 bits with zero violations. A blind scan of all lag pairs up to 600 rediscovers exactly its recurrence and nothing else.
findings.evidence: Zero violations in 49,999,750 tests per bit for j = 1..32, against 0.500 for MT19937, MINSTD and the rest. Lag scan (179,700 pairs, 20,000 words): only (103, 250) and (206, 500) are hit, the latter being the square of the trinomial $x^{250}+x^{103}+1$ over GF(2). Both have F = 0 and z = -800; every other pair has $|z|\le4.27$, and the sd of z is 1.004.

findings.claim: The logistic-map output is, bit for bit, a one-place shift of the previous output: $b_j(n)=b_{j+1}(n-1)\oplus b_1(n-1)$. So each 53-bit output carries at most about 5 new bits, yet the standard per-bit lag-1 test is blind to this.
findings.evidence: N = 5e7 (double): zero violations for j = 1..26; j = 27: 6; j = 40: 24,370 (4.9e-4); j = 52: 0.36. Summing the binary entropy of the violation rates gives at most 4.12 + 1 = 5.1 bits of new information per output. Per-bit lag-1 |z| < 6, and that small excess is consistent with inflation by the 5.6e6 cycle. REAL*4: violations below 1e-4 for j <= 11 (j = 4: 1 in 5e7).

findings.claim: In double precision, MINSTD bits 32 to 53 are a copy of bits 1 to 22, because $k/(2^{31}-1)$ has a binary expansion of period 31. The copy is broken only by the rounding carry at bit 53. The blind lag scan also detects it.
findings.evidence: Violations of $b_j=b_{j-31}$: 10 in 5e7 at j = 32 (2.0e-7), rising as $\tfrac13 2^{-(53-j)}$ to 0.333 at j = 53 (16,669,531). MT19937 control: 0.500. The per-bit frequency z of bits 32..53 repeats that of bits 1..22. Lag-scan sd of z = 1.033 against the predicted $\sqrt{34/32}=1.031$ (bit 32 of the 32-bit word equals bit 1).

findings.claim: Bit 49 of the MINSTD double carries a weak but reproducible lag-1 correlation, $r\approx5\times10^{-4}$. It comes from the rounding carry, which ties bit 49 to state bits 18 to 24, and not from bit 18 itself.
findings.evidence: z = 4.9 (N = 5e7), 6.9 (seed 777, N = 2e8), 7.1 (seed 4242, N = 2e8). Bit 18: z = 0.66. Carry indicator (2.08% of draws): z = -2.7. Pairwise cross terms: z = -1.8 and -0.9. The effect is therefore a higher-order dependence, mechanism only partly identified. No other MINSTD bit exceeds |z| = 2.8 at N = 2e8 for j <= 43.

findings.claim: Converting to REAL*4 produces its own bit-level signatures: bits beyond 24 are progressively empty, R250 bit 24 is biased by round-half-to-even, and LOGISTIC develops strong lag-1 correlations in bits 26 to 41.
findings.evidence: N = 5e7. $P(b_j=1)\approx\tfrac12 2^{-(j-24)}$ for j > 24 (j = 25: z = -3535, P = 0.25). R250 bit 24: z = -13.3, against -13.8 predicted from the $2^{-8}$ tie probability in [0.5, 1). LOGISTIC REAL*4 bits 26..41: r = 0.14 to 0.25, because a bit beyond 24 is set only when x is small and the tent map leaves 0 slowly (doubling each step). Double-precision dead bits: RAND 23..53, RANDU and RANDM 32..53, R250 33..53.

findings.claim: Test-design traps. Stuck bits make every lag pair look significant unless they are masked, and RANDU's periodic low bits make the masked scan too regular.
findings.evidence: Before masking constant bits, every one of the 179,700 pairs was flagged: RANDU and RANDM at z of about -25 (3 stuck bits) and RAND at about -250 (10 dead bits). After masking: RANDU sd of z = 0.726 and RANDM 0.722, against 1.006 for MT19937 and a prediction of $\sqrt{15/29}=0.719$ (14 of 29 live bits have period at most $2^{14}<L$ and contribute almost deterministic counts). Maximum |z| for RANDU is 3.18, against 4.6 for MT19937.

findings.claim: gfortran RAND() is exactly $\lfloor (k-1)/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$, where $k$ is the Park-Miller state. This refines the shared fact that RAND is MINSTD truncated to a multiple of $2^{-22}$.
findings.evidence: Over 1e8 draws, the formula $\lfloor (k-1)/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$ has 0 mismatches. Both $\lfloor k2^{22}/M\rfloor/2^{22}$ and $\lfloor k/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$ have 195,385 mismatches (0.195%, about 1/512). Consequently RAND bits 1..22 differ from the MINSTD double's bits in up to 494 of 5e7 draws per bit.

figures.caption: Signed significance of the digit-frequency $\chi^2$ test (9 dof, $N=10^8$) at each decimal position $p$. Red is non-uniform, blue is too uniform, and near-white is consistent with uniform. Exact digits fail at a depth set by each generator's resolution: RAND at 10, R250 at 21, RANDU and RANDM at 17 after a too-uniform band at $p=5$ to $14$. Naive extraction $\mathrm{mod}(\lfloor x\,10^p\rfloor,10)$ fails for every generator at $p=16$ in double and $p=8$ in REAL*4. LOGISTIC fails everywhere at $10^8$ draws because of its cycle, but passes on its first $10^7$ outputs.

Measured digit $\chi^2$ against decimal position (markers) compared with the exact resolution model (dashed): $9+\lambda_p$ for a uniform $B$-bit lattice, the deterministic full-period $\lambda_p$ for RANDU and RANDM, and a binade enumeration for REAL*4. The gray band is the two-sided acceptance region at $10^{-4}$. Every dyadic generator fails near $p=B-11$, far deeper than $B\log_{10}2$, while the exact rational digits of MINSTD never fail.

Bit-plane images: rows are the first 128 outputs and columns are bits $j=1$ to $53$ of the double (black = 1). Dead bits start after 22 (RAND), 31 (RANDU, RANDM) and 32 (R250). LOGISTIC shows a diagonal pattern because each row is the previous row shifted one bit left. The RANDU zoom shows bits 29 and 31 stuck, bit 30 alternating, and the period-4 and period-8 bits 28 and 27.

Per-bit frequency of ones (top) and lag-1 autocorrelation (bottom) in double (left) and REAL*4 (right) for $N=5\times10^7$; color is the signed $\log_{10}(1/p)$ and gray marks bits that never change. The LCG low bits are strongly correlated (RANDU bits 16 to 27 have $r\approx1/3$), and REAL*4 progressively empties the bits beyond 24. MT19937, RANNUM and R250 pass everywhere; MINSTD passes except for a weak effect in bit 49.

Exact low-order structure of RANDU and RANDM. (a) The measured period of bit $j$ equals $2^{30-j}$. (b) The period of decimal digit $p$ equals $2^{30-p}$. (c) Lag-1 bit autocorrelation, measured (markers) and computed over the full residue orbit (dashed); the $1/3$ plateau comes from $65539\equiv3 \pmod{2^{16}}$. (d) The Berlekamp-Massey linear complexity equals $2^{29-j}+1$.

Hidden bit identities. (a) R250 obeys its recurrence in every bit with zero violations, while the controls give 1/2. (b) The logistic output is a one-bit shift of the previous output, exactly in bits 1 to 26. (c) MINSTD doubles copy bits 1 to 22 into bits 32 to 53, broken only by the rounding carry $\tfrac13 2^{-(53-j)}$. (d) A blind scan of 179,700 lag pairs flags only the two R250 lags; it also shows RANDU's too-narrow $z$ distribution and MINSTD's slightly wide one.

Berlekamp-Massey linear complexity profiles $L(n)$. A random-looking stream follows $n/2$ (RANNUM). R250 saturates at 250, MT19937 at 19937, and RANDU bits 16 and 24 at 8193 and 33, so each of those bit streams is exactly predictable by a linear feedback shift register after $2L$ observed bits.

caveats: Sample sizes differ by test: the bit-level tests used N = 5e7 (MINSTD rechecked at 2e8), not 1e8; the lag scan used L = 20,000 words and lags up to 600; Berlekamp-Massey used L = 50,000 bits, so RANDU bits j <= 14 (complexity above 25,000) cannot saturate.
LOGISTIC results at N = 5e7 and 1e8 include about 6 and 15 repetitions of its 5,638,349-step cycle, which inflates its statistics. Only the first-1e7 rows are clean digit tests of LOGISTIC.
MIDSQ was seeded with 12345678 because seed 777 collapses to 0 after two steps. With 12345678 it enters a 100-cycle after 10,352 steps, so all MIDSQ results describe that cycle.

The REAL*4 prediction assumes a continuous uniform source rounded to nearest. It ignores that RANDU values below 2^-7 are exact in REAL*4 (so B = 31 there) and the binade-boundary weights; both effects are negligible at the measured depths.

The too-uniform significances for RANDU and RANDM depend on the ratio of N to the digit periods $2^{30-p}$, so they change with N. They are deterministic properties of the sequence, not sampling fluctuations.

The MINSTD bit-49 correlation (z about 7 at N = 2e8) is reproducible over two seeds, but its mechanism is only partly identified: it is not pairwise and appears to be a higher-order dependence exposed by the rounding carry.

Multiple testing: roughly 1,500 heat-map cells are evaluated at |S| > 4, so about 0.15 false alarms are expected overall. Isolated cells with 4 < S < 6 should be read together with the model prediction.

Planned but not done: joint (pair) digit tests and a conditional-entropy test of $d_p$ given the prefix, which would detect resolution near $p\approx B\log_{10}2$ rather than $B-11$; repeats of the digit heat map over several seeds; raster images of single bit streams; the exact Games-Chan complexity for the periodic bits.
rnd_test_claude.f was not modified (it belongs to the hist family). Scratch outputs (about 22 MB, largest file 1.1 MB) are in tests/digits/out.
rnglib_issues: No implementation bug found. Exact-digit counts for MT19937, RANDU and MINSTD were reproduced independently in Python, and numpy RandomState(777).random_sample reproduces rnglib's MT19937 for seed 777 exactly.

Correction to the shared verified fact about RAND: gfortran RAND() equals $\lfloor (k-1)/2^9\rfloor/2^{22}$ with $k$ the Park-Miller state (0 mismatches in 1e8 draws). Truncating $k/(2^{31}-1)$ down to a multiple of $2^{-22}$ disagrees in 195,385 of 1e8 draws (1/512). It still has exactly $2^{22}$ possible values.

Usage hazard: rng_init(G_MIDSQ, 777_8) collapses to the absorbing state 0 after two steps ($777^2=603729\to60\to0$). The 8-digit seeds 12345678, 31415926, 77777777 and 98765432 all fall into the same 100-cycle (containing 86560000) after tails of 1,787 to 12,139 steps.

Usage hazard: the LOGISTIC generator from seed 777 enters a cycle of length 5,638,349 after a tail of 14,324,259 steps (Brent's algorithm on a replica of the state that is bit-exact against rnglib for 1e6 steps). Any family drawing more than about 2e7 LOGISTIC numbers is testing a repeated block.

Behavior note, not a bug: with rng_single=.true., IEEE round-half-to-even biases R250's REAL*4 bit 24 ($P(1)\approx\tfrac12-2^{-10}$, z = -13.3 at N = 5e7). rng_single has no effect on RAND, whose values already fit in 22 bits.
